messages:
Mira Chen: quick idea — instead of a single global eviction watermark, what if we maintain per-tenant "pagewatermarks" that drive a gentle rebalancer?
Alex D: curious — is this just another threshold or a periodic background mover? :thinking_face: 
Mira Chen: both. watermark = moving quantile of resident pages per-tenant. rebalancer runs incremental migrations + compaction when tenant crosses soft guard. goal is lower fragmentation without big synchronous evicts.
Jiang Wu: how does this avoid noisy neighbors? if tenant A warms up and bumps watermark, could it starve B?
Mira Chen: plan is to enforce a global warm_reserve and also a fairness token bucket so rebalancer schedules work proportional to tenant priority/commit. fairness tokens refill based on tenancy-weighted window.
Samir Patel: worried about latency spikes when migrations run during tail requests. do we throttle based on p99?
Mira Chen: yes — we gate migration throughput by observed tokenized p95/p99 tail. default: block background migration if p99 > 150ms for > 30s.
Rachel (eng-runtime): what about integration with existing residency telemetry? we need signals for hotness, fragmentation, migration success rates, and rollback hooks.
Mira Chen: agreed. telemetry stub: hot_ratio, frag_index, migration_success, migration_latency. we'll expose a per-tenant dashboard and an opt-in alert that flips the rebalancer into conservative mode.
Alex D: show me config prototype?
Mira Chen: sure — rough YAML prototype:
```
pagewatermark:
  tenant_window: 10m
  hot_threshold: 0.65   # quantile to consider pages hot
  cold_threshold: 0.25  # below this we demote
  rebalance_action: migrate   # migrate | compact | demote
  migrate_rate_limit: 50MB/s
  p99_pause_ms: 150
  warm_reserve_pct: 0.08
```
Jiang Wu: migrate_rate_limit should be token-bucketed per-node and burstable for low-latency scenarios. also add a max-concurrent-migrations parameter.
Samir Patel: and add a safety check: if migration raises CPU by X% or grpc queue length increases, revert in-flight and backoff exponentially.
Mira Chen: good call. will add CPU and queue heuristics to the safety checks.
Rachel (eng-runtime): rollout plan? feature gate + canary on Dedicated GPUs first?
Mira Chen: yes — feature flag + dry-run mode where rebalancer only logs planned actions. then small canary group of tenants on Dedicated, monitor metrics, then broaden.
Alex D: operator commands?
Mira Chen: initial CLI: `rbctl preview --tenant=acme --dry-run` and `rbctl apply --tenant=acme --rate=20MB/s`
Samir Patel: please include an emergency kill switch: `rbctl pause-all` + API to pause per-tenant.
Mira Chen: yep.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment queued: rebalancer-v1 -> staging (id: canary-32412). ETA: 12m :rocket:
Alex D: :eyes: I'll watch canary metrics. if frag index drops without p99 regressions we merge.
Jiang Wu: one more long-term thought — we should design the rebalancer hooks so other schedulers (compaction service, prefetch controller) can subscribe; avoid hard-coding actions.
Mira Chen: agreed — plugin hooks for actions. plan is prototype in runtime, then surface plugin API for platform services.
Rachel (eng-runtime): ok sounds like next steps: 1) prototype in a branch (Mira + Jiang) 2) add telemetry + dashboard (Rachel) 3) safety & operator CLI (Samir) 4) canary testing (Alex)
Mira Chen: I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with the YAML, pseudo-code, and test plan. tagging owners in the PR. :+1:
Alex D: SGTM
Samir Patel: 👍
Jiang Wu: 👍
Rachel (eng-runtime): 👍
